programs.title: Career development
lead: Résumé-review workshops, career-preparation sessions and professional panels give students a way to test their materials and plans against what working professionals look for. Each format is meant to leave a student with something to act on: a revised résumé, a clearer picture of a role, a person to follow up with.
points: Career preparation for internships and full-time roles

programs.title: Industry access
lead: Company information sessions, industry panels and joint company tours put students in the same room as people doing the work, and show them more than one technical and professional path. Our chapter hosted an LPL Financial x MTC SDSU informational session in October 2025, covered in the next section.
points: Relationships with professionals and company representatives

programs.title: Community and belonging
lead: Not everything the chapter does is career-driven. Social events and regular contact give Muslim students interested in technology a place to meet and support each other, across majors and years. Those relationships are what keep members involved after a single event or recruiting cycle.
points: A campus space for Muslim students interested in technology
Connections that last beyond one event

programs.title: Community technology and service
lead: The chapter works with local masajid and Muslim community organizations to find volunteer opportunities and to match student skills with community needs. Some of that work is building products, such as websites, for organizations that may not have a technical team of their own.
This is the part of the chapter that points outward: it helps students find opportunities, and it gives them a way to use their skills for others.
points: Volunteer opportunities with local masajid and community organizations
Websites and other technical products for community partners
Support for organizations without dedicated technical teams
